changes.year1_quote: We are exposed to market risks, including changes to foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, and equity investment risk.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We are exposed to market risks, including changes to foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, and equity price risk.
changes.reasoning: The same three market risks (FX, interest rate, and equity) are disclosed in materially identical language; "equity investment risk" vs "equity price risk" is a cosmetic wording change describing the same underlying exposure.
changes.title: Overview of Market Risk Exposures

changes.year1_quote: We have foreign currency risks related to our revenue and operating expenses denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar, primarily the Euro. Accordingly, changes in exchange rates, and in particular a strengthening of the U.S. dollar, have in the past, and may in the future, negatively affect our revenue
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We have foreign currency risks related to our revenue and operating expenses denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar, primarily the Euro. Accordingly, changes in exchange rates, and in particular a strengthening of the U.S. dollar, have negatively affected, and may continue to negatively affect, our revenue and other operating results as expressed in U.S. dollars.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 discloses the identical economic risk (FX exposure on Euro-denominated revenue and operating expenses) with materially the same language; the only change is a slightly firmer framing ("have negatively affected, and may continue to") plus an added cross-reference, which is not a softening.
changes.title: Foreign Currency Exchange Risk — Revenue and Expenses

changes.year1_quote: We have experienced and will continue to experience fluctuations in our net income as a result of transaction gains or losses related to revaluing monetary asset and liability balances that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency... we have not entered into... derivatives
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We have experienced and will continue to experience fluctuations in our net income as a result of transaction gains or losses related to revaluing monetary asset and liability balances that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency... we have not entered into... derivatives
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 is materially identical language describing the same foreign currency transaction gain/loss risk and unchanged hedging posture (no derivatives entered). Only the disclosed loss figures rolled forward to updated periods, which is a routine numeric update rather than a substantive change in risk.
changes.title: Foreign Currency Transaction Gains/Losses and Hedging

changes.year1_quote: A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in interest rates would have resulted in a decrease of $714 million and $794 million in the market value of our available-for-sale debt securities as of December 31, 2021 and December 31, 2020, respectively.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in market interest rates would have resulted in a decrease of $558 million and $714 million in the market value of our available-for-sale debt securities and cash equivalents as of December 31, 2022 and 2021, respectively.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 discloses the same interest-rate sensitivity on cash and marketable securities using materially identical methodology and language; only the updated sensitivity figures and an added reference to current unrealized losses changed, reflecting normal period-over-period quantitative updates rather than a change in the underlying risk.
changes.title: Interest Rate Sensitivity — Cash and Marketable Securities

changes.year1_quote: Our equity investments are subject to a wide variety of market-related risks that could have a material impact on the carrying value of our holdings. We continually evaluate our equity investments in privately-held companies.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our equity investments are substantially all in non-marketable equity securities and are subject to equity price risks that could have a material impact on the carrying value of our holdings.
changes.reasoning: The same underlying economic risk — exposure of privately-held/non-marketable equity investments to market/price risk affecting carrying value — persists in Year-2022, with Candidate 1 mirroring the Year-1 language and Candidate 2 elaborating on valuation and impairment of the same holdings. The risk is materially unchanged.
changes.title: Equity Investment Risk — Privately-Held Companies Overview

changes.year1_quote: Volatility in the global economic climate and financial markets, including recent and ongoing effects related to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, which requires significant judgments, could result in a material impairment charge on our equity investments.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Uncertainties in the global economic climate and financial markets could adversely impact the valuation of these companies we invest in and, therefore, result in a material impairment or downward adjustment in our investments.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk (potential material impairment of privately-held equity investments due to economic/market conditions) is retained in Candidate 1, but the language is hedged: "Volatility...could result in a material impairment" is downgraded to "Uncertainties...could adversely impact...result in a material impairment or downward adjustment," and the specific COVID-19 driver plus "requires significant judgments" qualifier were dropped, weakening the disclosure.
changes.title: Equity Investment Valuation, Impairment Assessment, and Carrying Value

changes.year1_quote: For additional information about our equity investments, see Note 1 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, Note 5 — Equity Investments, and Note 6 — Fair Value Measurements in the notes to the consolidated financial statements...
changes.year2_quote_or_null: For additional information, see Note 1 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, Note 6 — Non-marketable Equity Securities, Note 7 — Fair Value Measurements, and Note 11 — Long-term Debt in the notes to the consolidated financial statements...
changes.reasoning: The Year-1 unit was a pure cross-reference pointer to financial statement notes for equity investments. In Year-2 this same cross-reference function is preserved but broadened into a single consolidated pointer covering equity securities plus additional topics (long-term debt), folding the equity-investment reference into a wider disclosure. The underlying equity investment risk itself is substantively addressed in Candidates 2 and 3.
changes.title: Equity Investment Risk — Cross-References to Financial Statement Notes
